p: Thinking of turning up as a big group? Ask about group options when you book, and consider splitting into smaller teams so you're not queuing at every hole. It also sets up a cheeky team-against-team contest. Turn up a few minutes before your tee time, grab a drink and let the trash talk begin.

Crazy golf can be surprisingly tense when there are bragging rights at stake, so agree the rules before you start. Do mulligans count? Is there a forfeit for the loser? A bit of daft structure can make a round even more fun, especially with a competitive bunch of mates.

Once your round's done, Leeds has a brilliant spread of food and drink. Call Lane and the surrounding streets are packed with bars and restaurants, while the Corn Exchange is a beautiful Victorian building with independent shops worth a nosey during the day. Trinity Leeds is the big shopping centre, with a food hall and plenty of places to eat.

If you're making a day of it, Roundhay Park is one of the city's much-loved green spaces and home to Tropical World, where you can see butterflies, meerkats and reptiles. Kirkstall Abbey's atmospheric ruins are free to explore and lovely on a sunny afternoon. Harewood House, a grand country estate just outside Leeds, makes a great day trip if you've got a car.
